ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: What happens to the mayfly population if the trout population disappears?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The food web diagram shows Leaves & Algae on the left with arrows pointing toward Mayflies, Stoneflies, and Caddis Flies. There are arrows from Mayflies toward Trout, from Stoneflies toward Trout, and from Caddis Flies toward Trout. There is also an arrow from Trout toward Humans. Reasoning: The arrow from Mayflies to Trout indicates that trout eat mayflies. If the trout population disappears, mayflies would have less predation pressure from trout. With fewer predators eating them, the mayfly population would tend to increase.
